questions.question: What does typeof null return?
questions.explanation: A long-standing language quirk makes typeof null return "object".

questions.question: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that cannot be reassigned?
questions.explanation: const creates a block-scoped binding that cannot be reassigned.

questions.question: What is the result of "5" + 3?
questions.explanation: With a string operand, + performs string concatenation.

questions.question: Which array method adds an element to the end of an array?
questions.explanation: push appends elements to the end and returns the new length.

questions.question: What does 0 === "0" evaluate to?
questions.explanation: Strict equality does not coerce types, and number differs from string.

questions.question: Which method converts a JSON string into a JavaScript object?
questions.explanation: JSON.parse parses JSON text into a value; stringify does the reverse.

questions.question: Which value is falsy?
questions.explanation: 0 is falsy; non-empty strings and all objects, including empty arrays, are truthy.

questions.question: Which method returns the first element matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector returns the first matching element (or null).

questions.question: What does [10, 1, 2].sort() return?
questions.explanation: Without a comparator, sort compares elements as strings, and "10" < "2".

questions.question: What does [1, 2, 3, 4].filter(n => n % 2).reduce((s, n) => s + n, 0) return?
questions.explanation: filter keeps odd numbers [1, 3], and reduce sums them to 4.

questions.question: How do arrow functions treat this?
options: They bind this to the arrow function itself
this is always the global object
this is set by the caller like regular functions
They use this from the enclosing lexical scope
questions.explanation: Arrow functions have no own this binding; they capture it lexically.

questions.question: What does console.log([] + {}) print?
questions.explanation: Both operands convert to strings: "" + "[object Object]".

questions.question: When does Promise.all([p1, p2, p3]) reject?
options: Only when all input promises reject
As soon as any one of the input promises rejects
Never; it collects rejections into the result array
Only after all promises have settled
questions.explanation: Promise.all rejects with the first rejection reason; Promise.allSettled waits for all.
